title: {{NAME}} and the Golden Boot
moral: The greatest trophies are not made of gold, they are made of what you gave to earn them.

pages.content:
The Golden Boot was the kingdom's most prestigious football award, and it had not been given to a young player in forty years.

Princess Elara was on the selection committee. She had read every match report from the junior leagues that season.

One player stood out: a midfielder whose match data was exceptional but whose best work was invisible in the statistics. Setting things up. Creating space. Making others better.

She asked to see him play.

{{NAME}} played without knowing he was being watched. He played the way he always played: for the team.

pages.content:
The unicorn was the unexpected element.

Every match day, a unicorn appeared at the edge of the pitch and watched. Not the same spot: different positions, as if it was studying the match from different angles.

"What is that?" asked Princess Elara's advisor.

"I don't know," she said. "But it's watched every one of his matches for three months."

After the match, {{NAME}} walked over to the unicorn and they stood together for a moment, not speaking, just existing in the same space.

"They know each other," said the advisor.

"Yes," said the princess.

pages.content:
She called {{NAME}} to her offices and asked directly: "Tell me about the unicorn."

"She was at my first match," he said. "Two years ago. I played terribly. She came back the next week. I played less terribly. She kept coming."

"Has she ever guided you?"

"No. She watches. But knowing she's watching makes me play the way I want to play, not the way I think I should play. The difference is important."

Princess Elara thought about this for a long time.

"That's what the best audiences do," she said finally.

pages.content:
She awarded him the Golden Boot at the season ceremony.

In her citation, she said: "This player makes others better. His statistics don't show it. His matches do. A game is better for his presence in it, and so is any team."

The unicorn was at the ceremony, standing at the back of the hall.

When {{NAME}} received the boot, the unicorn's horn pulsed once: gold, warm, brief.

"She approves," said someone near {{NAME}}.

"She approves every time," he said quietly. "That's why I play the way I play."

pages.content:
He walked home with the Golden Boot under his arm and the memory of the horn's pulse warm in his chest.

Two years of matches. One set of watching eyes that made him play his best.

He thought about what the princess had said: the best audiences make you better.

He put the boot on his shelf and lay in bed looking at it.

The unicorn was probably in the park meadow now, watching the stars.

He fell asleep feeling watched in the best possible way.
